pairs: et suis spatiis transeunt universa sub cælo.
and all things under heaven continue during their interval.
et tempus evellendi quod plantatum est.
and a time to pull up what was planted.
and a time to build up.
et tempus longe fieri ab amplexibus.
and a time to be far from embraces.
and a time to cast away.
Quid habet amplius homo de labore suo?
What more does a man have from his labor?
Vidi afflictionem quam dedit Deus filiis hominum,
I have seen the affliction that God has given to the sons of men,
in order that they may be occupied by it.
Cuncta fecit bona in tempore suo,
He has made all things good in their time,
and he has handed over the world to their disputes,
ut non inveniat homo opus quod operatus est Deus ab initio usque ad finem.
so that man may not discover the work which God made from the beginning, even until the end.
Et cognovi quod non esset melius nisi lætari,
And I realize that there is nothing better than to rejoice,
et facere bene in vita sua;
and to do well in this life.
omnis enim homo qui comedit et bibit,
For this is a gift from God:
et videt bonum de labore suo,
when each man eats and drinks,
and sees the good results of his labor.
Didici quod omnia opera quæ fecit Deus perseverent in perpetuum;
I have learned that all the works which God has made continue on, in perpetuity.
We are not able to add anything, nor to take anything away,
nec auferre, quæ fecit Deus ut timeatur.
from those things which God has made in order that he may be feared.
What is in the future, has already existed.
And God restores what has passed away.
Vidi sub sole in loco judicii impietatem,
I saw under the sun: instead of judgment, impiety,
And I said in my heart:
“God will judge the just and the impious,
et tempus omnis rei tunc erit.
and then the time for each matter shall be.”
Dixi in corde meo de filiis hominum,
I said in my heart, about the sons of men,
and reveal them to be like wild animals.
Idcirco unus interitus est hominis et jumentorum,
For this reason, the passing away of man and of beasts is one,
and the condition of both is equal.
et nihil habet homo jumento amplius:
and man has nothing more than beast;
for all these are subject to vanity.
et omnia pergunt ad unum locum.
And all things continue on to one place;
for from the earth they were made,
and unto the earth they shall return together.
Quis novit si spiritus filiorum Adam ascendat sursum,
Who knows if the spirit of the sons of Adam ascend upward,
et si spiritus jumentorum descendat deorsum?
and if the spirit of the beasts descend downward?
Et deprehendi nihil esse melius quam lætari hominem in opere suo,
And I have discovered nothing to be better than for a man to rejoice in his work:
for this is his portion. And who shall add to him,
Quis enim eum adducet ut post se futura cognoscat?
so that he may know the things that will occur after him?
